reason: Use Tier 2: decouple input-history embeddings from output-item embeddings within the successful masked transformer. Masked reconstruction reached 0.5800, while relative attention bias and R-Drop reduced HR@10 to 0.5725 and 0.5650; this favors preserving the masked representation while testing a different component. Tied embeddings may constrain performance because representing historical context and discriminating recommendation targets impose different requirements, although the trajectory does not establish this as the cause of the plateau.

plan.model_design: Starting from the original 0.5800 masked-model configuration, make one architectural change: introduce an independently trainable output_emb table for target and candidate scoring while retaining item_emb for sequence inputs. Initialize output_emb by cloning the initialized item_emb weights without advancing the random-number generator, preserving initial predictions while allowing the two representations to specialize during training. Use output_emb consistently for positive logits, the existing 256 sampled negatives, and predict scores, retaining the jointly trained item_bias and original single-pass sampled-softmax objective without R-Drop or relative bias. Preserve MaskedSASRec.__init__, forward(sequence), predict(sequence, candidates), prediction_sequence, existing variable names, masking, loss weighting, and all other hyperparameters; both embedding tables belong to one jointly trained network per category.
plan.training_evaluation: Update architecture_spec, validate_metadata, and write_predict_script to record the untied embedding architecture and strictly load output_emb alongside every other parameter from exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Preserve supplied splits, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, worker seeding, optimizer, early stopping, SASREC_EPOCHS default 200, and trial-local artifacts. Keep fixed validation with 200 users per category and 99 unique negatives using evaluation seed 42, select checkpoints by the existing HR@10/NDCG ordering, and report the selected checkpoints' actual macro HR@10 against the 0.5800 reference. Check that input and output weights initially match but have distinct storage and receive gradients, then verify exported predictor scores against the same selected checkpoint using identical history processing; retain single-GPU execution, the final validation-score print, and host-managed held-out inference without accessing test files or creating a synthetic submission.
